# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 74 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 74 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_074_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Part 1 — The Great Rock and the Gate

**74:1** After I had written down the commandments and similitudes of the shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me and said: "I want to show you all the things the Holy Spirit spoke with you in the form of the church. For that Spirit is the Son of God."

**74:2** "For you are feeble in the flesh, and the truth was not yet explained to you. Speak with the Power and it will come to you clearly, since that Power is strong and divine and belongs to glorious and mighty virtue."

**74:3** And I said to him: "Lord, I beg you to show me all the things you promised to show me." And he led me to Arcadia, to a certain hill, and had me sit down on the hill. And he himself stood before me.

**74:4** And I saw a great plain, and around the plain twelve mountains, all having different forms. The first mountain had black rocks. The second was bare, with no vegetation. The third was full of thorns and brambles. The fourth had the grasses half-withered — the upper parts of the plants were green and the roots were dry, and some of the grasses were withered as the sun scorched them. The fifth mountain had green grass and was rugged. The sixth mountain was full of clefts, some small and some large, and in the clefts there was grass.

**74:5** The seventh mountain had smiling vegetation, and the whole mountain was flourishing, and cattle and birds of all kinds were feeding on that mountain; and the more the cattle and the birds fed, the more the mountain's vegetation flourished. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and from those springs every kind of creature of the Lord drank.

**74:6** The ninth mountain had no water at all and was entirely desert, and it was full of wild beasts and deadly reptiles that destroyed human beings. The tenth mountain had great trees and was entirely shaded, and beneath those trees sheep lay resting and chewing their cud.

**74:7** The eleventh mountain was covered with trees, and those trees were full of various fruits, so that anyone seeing them would desire to eat of their fruits. The twelfth mountain was entirely white and its appearance was cheerful, and the mountain was very beautiful in form.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the twelve-mountain vision that opens the elaborate allegory of Similitude 9.*
